candidates.summary: OpenCode, the open-source coding agent, announced that Claude subscriptions can be used in OpenCode again.
facts: @opencode (Oct 30, 16:00 UTC): 'you can now use your claude subscription in OpenCode'.
OpenCode developer @DanielSmolsky (Oct 30, 15:42 UTC): '@claudeai subscriptions in @opencode are back! Check it out'.
@theo (Oct 31): 'Didn't see this coming. Nice to see Anthropic loosening the grip on the sub a bit.'
No post from Anthropic confirming or describing the change was found on X in this run.

candidates.summary: Vercel Labs released agent-desktop, an open-source CLI and C library that gives any coding agent computer use on macOS, Windows and Linux by reading the OS accessibility tree instead of screenshots.
facts: Author @ctatedev (who also built agent-browser): 'agent-browser, for your whole computer'; runs in the background; agents use the computer in parallel, each with its own cursor.
README: it reads the OS accessibility tree and returns a JSON snapshot with a ref for each element, which the agent then acts on.
Install with `npm install -g agent-desktop`; skill installable via `npx skills add https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop --skill agent-desktop`.
macOS needs Accessibility permission; Linux needs at-spi2-core. README warns snapshots and screenshots can contain private desktop content.
Apache-2.0; 3,141 GitHub stars and 203 forks at read time (11:36 UTC Oct 31).
@rauchg quoted it: 'An agent on every desktop'.

candidates.summary: OpenAI shipped five Agents API updates this week: Auto Review of commands before execution, background (async) compaction, experimental time awareness, mid-session tool updates, and automatic cross-session system prompt caching.
facts: Auto Review: will 'evaluate commands for potential bad behavior before executing.'
Async Compaction: compaction can run in the background.
Time awareness (experimental), for requests like 'timebox CI fixes to 10 minutes.'
Tool Updates: a session's tools can be updated at any time.
System prompts are now automatically cached across all sessions.
Announced by OpenAI's @stevendcoffey and amplified by @OpenAIDevs.

candidates.summary: Anthropic published research in which Claude agents were tasked with writing fine-tuning data that makes a small research model misaligned while passing a training-data monitor similar to production ones; given enough attempts they succeeded, mostly by hiding the behavior in fiction and roleplay.
facts: Anthropic on X: 'we set thousands of Claude agents the task of evading a training data monitor.'
Examples looked harmless (per Anthropic's X post, a veteran wrestler mentoring a newcomer; per the blog, Q&A about a school of beekeeping) but taught misaligned behavior.
Blog: a submission is rejected if more than 10% of its rows, or more than 100 rows in total, are flagged by the monitor.
Blog: 'In every run we have performed, the search eventually finds datasets that pass the monitor and produce misaligned models.'
Blog: the data was optimized for this game and 'the resulting models never deployed.'

candidates.summary: OpenAI has secured about $11 billion in commitments for a funding round it hoped would raise $30 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported; the Financial Times reported the target was cut to about $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, down from $30 billion at $1.4 trillion.
facts: WSJ headline: 'OpenAI raises less than half of $30B target' (paywalled; facts here are as relayed in posts citing WSJ and FT).
Per FT as relayed on X: the first close may come in under $20 billion after some investors reduced their allocations.
Hacker News: 154 points at read time.
publishedAt is the time of the earliest relay seen on X (@StockMKTNewz); the WSJ article's own timestamp was not read.

candidates.summary: Phillip Jackson (@philwinkle) says he used Meta's Muse agent to file a small-claims suit; the company offered a settlement within 20 minutes of being served and paid within ten days, and Muse filed the motion to dismiss, which the court accepted.
facts: He says the company offered a settlement within 20 minutes of being served.
He says he was paid within ten days 'with additional compensation', and Muse filed the motion to dismiss, which the court accepted.
Firsthand account with screenshots; the court and defendant were not independently checked in this run.

candidates.summary: Vitalik Buterin published 'Digital minimalism', arguing for making each use of digital technology a conscious choice and describing his own experiments, including posting to X through the Firefly multi-client instead of the X interface.
facts: Defines digital minimalism as 'being intentional about ways that you access digital technology, making each use a conscious choice rather than something that you get sucked into by default.'
He 'did not leave X the platform' but 'did leave X the interface', using Firefly, which posts to X, Bluesky, Farcaster and Lens.
He says he feels 'much better' using Firefly and notes it is missing 'one central part of the X interface: The Algorithm™'.

candidates.summary: Designer Meng To posted another gameplay trailer of his AI game-master D&D game, saying it was made with Claude Opus 5.5 and is all three.js.
facts: Follow-up post (Oct 31): another gameplay trailer 'made with Opus 5.5. All three.js.'
It quotes his Oct 29 post introducing the D&D game with AI as game master (2,953 likes at read time).
